name: Crockpot Creamy Tomato Chicken Pasta
steps: Put chicken in the Crockpot. Sprinkle with Italian seasoning and garlic powder, then pour both jars of sauce over it.
Cover and cook on LOW 4-5 hours or HIGH 2-3 hours, until the thickest part of the chicken hits 165°F.
Remove chicken, shred with two forks, and stir it back into the sauce.
Boil pasta separately until al dente. Drain and stir into the Crockpot. Loosen with a splash of pasta water if thick.
Top with Parmesan if you like.
notes: Picky-eater tip: pull plain shredded chicken and buttered noodles for anyone who balks at the sauce. Save a mug of pasta water before draining.

name: Creamy Salsa Verde Chicken
steps: Put chicken in slow cooker, sprinkle with taco seasoning, pour salsa verde over.
Cook LOW 4-6 hr until 165°F. Remove and shred.
Cube cream cheese and whisk into hot salsa (cover 10 min to soften if needed). Stir chicken back in, squeeze in lime. Serve in tacos or over rice.
notes: Picky-eater tip: pull plain chicken before adding salsa-cream sauce; serve as a DIY taco bar.

name: Pepperoncini Italian Beef
steps: Put roast in slow cooker. Sprinkle au jus mix and Italian seasoning. Pour broth and ⅓ cup pepperoncini brine around it; add peppers and butter.
Cook LOW 8-9 hr until it pulls apart.
Shred, discard big fat pieces, stir back into juices. Pile onto toasted hoagies with provolone; serve juice for dipping.
notes: Mild flavor—pepperoncini don't make it spicy. Keep peppers off kids' sandwiches.

name: White Chicken Chili
steps: Add everything except lime and toppings (beans drained/rinsed, onion diced, garlic minced). Cook LOW 5-6 hr until chicken is 165°F.
Remove and shred chicken. Mash ~1 cup beans against the pot to thicken.
Stir chicken back in, add lime juice, salt to taste. Serve with toppings.
notes: Kids usually like it with lots of cheese and chips crushed on top.

name: Creamy Ranch Chicken
steps: Add chicken, ranch seasoning, broth and pepper. Cook LOW until 165°F.
Remove and shred chicken.
Cube cream cheese, soften in hot broth ~10 min, whisk smooth, stir chicken back in. Serve over mashed potatoes or egg noodles.
notes: One of the most kid-friendly on the list.

name: Honey Garlic Chicken
steps: Whisk honey, soy, minced garlic and vinegar. Pour over thighs.
Cook LOW until tender and at least 165°F. Move chicken to a plate.
Boil cooking liquid in a saucepan. Mix cornstarch with 1 tbsp cold water, whisk in, simmer 1-2 min until glossy. Toss with chicken. Serve over rice with broccoli.

name: French Onion Chicken
steps: Thinly slice onions; sauté in butter over medium 10-15 min until soft and lightly browned.
Add onions, chicken, soup mix and broth to slow cooker. Cook LOW until 165°F.
Top with cheese, cover ~5 min to melt. Serve with onions and broth spooned over.
notes: Picky-eater tip: serve kids' portions with cheese but skip the onions.

name: BBQ Pulled Pork
steps: Put sliced onion and minced garlic in slow cooker. Rub pork with paprika and salt; set on top.
Add broth, vinegar and ½ cup BBQ sauce. Cook LOW 8-10 hr until it shreds easily.
Shred, discard big fat pieces, mix with remaining BBQ sauce and enough cooking liquid to stay juicy. Serve on buns with slaw.
notes: Uses pork shoulder (not tenderloin) so it stays juicy over the long cook.

name: Creamy Buffalo Chicken
steps: Add chicken, Buffalo sauce and ranch seasoning. Cook LOW until 165°F.
Shred chicken.
Stir cubed cream cheese into hot sauce until smooth, then stir chicken back in. Use for sliders, wraps, or loaded baked potatoes.
notes: Spicy. For kids, pull plain chicken before saucing, or make Ranch Chicken instead.

name: Creamy Tuscan Chicken
steps: Add chicken, broth, minced garlic, seasonings, and chopped sun-dried tomatoes. Cook LOW until 165°F; move chicken to a plate.
Whisk cubed cream cheese and Parmesan into hot liquid. Stir in spinach, cover 5-10 min to wilt.
Return chicken to sauce. Serve over pasta.
notes: Picky-eater tip: spinach and sun-dried tomatoes are easy to leave out of kids' bowls.

name: Italian Sausage & Peppers
steps: Brown sausage in oil in a skillet ~2 min per side.
Put sliced peppers and onion in slow cooker, sausage on top; add marinara, minced garlic and Italian seasoning.
Cook LOW 5-6 hr until peppers are tender and sausage is 160°F. Serve on hoagies or slice into sauce for pasta.
notes: Use mild sausage for the kids.

name: Baked Chicken Tenders, Potatoes & Green Beans
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Cut potatoes into small wedges, toss with oil and salt, roast 15 min.
Dip chicken in beaten egg, then in crumbs mixed with garlic powder. Bake on a separate pan 15-20 min until 165°F and potatoes are tender.
Steam the green beans.

name: Slow-Cooker Salsa Chicken Tacos
steps: Cook chicken, salsa and seasoning on LOW 4-6 hr, checking early for 165°F.
Shred chicken and stir back into sauce.
Serve in tortillas with cheese. Kids: chicken, cheese and tortilla separate on the plate.
notes: Double it (about 2½ lb chicken) to have 2 cups left for quesadillas or rice bowls the next night.

name: Chicken Quesadillas & Black Beans
steps: Fill tortillas with chicken and cheese, fold, and brown in a skillet over medium 2-3 min per side.
Warm drained beans and corn for a side.
Keep kids' plain; salsa at the table.

name: Chicken & Broccoli Pasta
steps: Cook pasta, adding broccoli for the last 3 min.
Melt butter, whisk in flour 1 min. Gradually whisk in milk and simmer until thick. Off heat, stir in cheddar.
Toss with pasta, broccoli and warmed chicken. Set plain pasta aside first for the kids if needed.

name: Chicken Fried Rice
steps: Scramble eggs in a large skillet; set aside.
Stir-fry vegetables in a little oil 3-4 min. Add rice, chicken and garlic powder; cook until hot.
Stir in eggs and soy sauce. Pull a kid portion before the soy if preferred.
notes: Best with day-old rice — cook extra rice earlier in the week.

name: Taco Bowls
steps: Brown meat, stir in taco seasoning and ¼ cup water, simmer 3 min.
Warm drained beans and corn.
Serve over rice with cheddar. Kids build their own from small piles.

name: Spaghetti with Meat Sauce
steps: Brown meat with garlic powder.
Add marinara and simmer 10 min while pasta cooks.
Serve with Parmesan. Plain pasta + sauce on the side for kids if needed.

name: Oven Meatballs, Mashed Potatoes & Peas
steps: Mix meat, egg, breadcrumbs, ¼ cup milk and garlic powder. Roll ~16 meatballs; bake at 400°F 15-20 min (beef 160°F, turkey 165°F).
Boil diced potatoes until tender; mash with butter and a splash of milk.
Heat peas and serve.
notes: Double the meatballs and freeze half for a future spaghetti or meatball-sub night.

name: Sloppy Joes & Potato Wedges
steps: Roast oiled potato wedges at 425°F 25-35 min, flipping halfway.
Brown meat, stir in tomato sauce, ketchup, mustard, Worcestershire and garlic powder; simmer 8-10 min.
Serve on buns, or filling next to a toasted bun for kids.

name: Cheeseburger Baked Potatoes
steps: Scrub and pierce potatoes; bake at 425°F 45-60 min until soft.
Brown meat with garlic powder.
Split potatoes, top with meat and cheese. Pickles and mustard at the table.
notes: Shortcut: microwave potatoes 8-10 min, then 10 min in the oven to crisp.

name: Sheet-Pan Sausage, Potatoes & Green Beans
steps: Cut potatoes bite-size, toss with oil and seasonings, roast at 425°F 20 min.
Add sliced sausage and green beans tossed with a little oil.
Roast 12-15 min more until potatoes are tender and sausage is hot.

name: Breakfast-for-Dinner Tacos
steps: Brown and crumble sausage.
Scramble eggs over medium-low.
Serve in warm tortillas with cheddar. Kids: eggs, sausage, fruit and tortilla separate.

name: Chicken Alfredo with Broccoli
steps: Boil pasta; add broccoli for the last 3 min. Save ½ cup pasta water, drain.
Warm Alfredo and chicken in the pot, loosen with pasta water.
Toss with pasta and broccoli, top with Parmesan.
notes: Kids who won't eat broccoli: steam it separately and serve on the side.

name: Build-Your-Own Naan Pizzas
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Set out naan, sauce, cheese, and toppings.
Everyone builds their own on a sheet pan.
Bake 8-10 min until cheese bubbles.
notes: Kids love making their own — great Friday night. Use leftover marinara from spaghetti or Crockpot pasta.

name: Grilled Cheese & Tomato Soup
steps: Heat soup in a pot.
Butter bread, fill with cheese, cook in a skillet over medium 2-3 min per side.
Cut into strips for dipping.
notes: Emergency backup dinner — keep soup in the pantry.

name: Teriyaki Chicken Rice Bowls
steps: Cut chicken into bite-size pieces; cook in a little oil over medium-high 6-8 min until 165°F.
Stir in teriyaki sauce and simmer 2 min until glossy.
Serve over rice with steamed veggies.
notes: Sweet sauce = usually a kid hit. Plain chicken + rice for the pickiest.

name: Sheet-Pan Nachos
steps: Heat oven to 400°F. Brown beef with taco seasoning and a splash of water.
Spread chips on a lined sheet pan; top with beef, drained beans, and cheese.
Bake 6-8 min until melted. Salsa and sour cream at the table.
notes: Make a 'kids' corner' with just chips, meat and cheese.

name: Baked Cheeseburger Sliders
steps: Heat oven to 350°F. Brown beef with garlic powder, salt and pepper; drain.
Slice rolls as one slab; put bottoms in a 9x13. Layer beef and cheese, add tops.
Brush with melted butter, cover with foil, bake 15 min. Bake fries alongside per bag.
notes: Ketchup/mustard/pickles at the table.

name: Stovetop Mac & Cheese with Ham & Peas
steps: Cook macaroni; add peas for the last 2 min. Drain.
Melt butter, whisk in flour 1 min, slowly whisk in milk and simmer until thick. Off heat stir in cheddar.
Stir in pasta, peas and ham.
notes: Leave ham and peas on the side for kids who want 'just mac'.

name: Easy Chicken Noodle Soup
steps: Sauté diced carrot, celery and onion in a little oil 5 min.
Add broth and thyme, simmer 10 min.
Add noodles and chicken, cook 6-8 min until noodles are tender. Salt to taste.
notes: Great in a thermos for lunches.

name: Crockpot Meatball Subs
steps: Dump frozen meatballs and marinara in the Crockpot. Cook LOW 4 hr or HIGH 2 hr.
Load into toasted rolls, top with cheese, broil 1-2 min to melt.
notes: 5-minute prep. Kids can have meatballs + bread on the side.

name: Crockpot Mississippi Pot Roast
steps: Put roast in Crockpot, sprinkle both packets over, top with butter (and pepperoncini if using). No liquid needed.
Cook LOW 8 hr until it shreds.
Serve over mashed potatoes with roasted or steamed carrots.
notes: Leftovers make great sandwiches or sliders. Skip pepperoncini for the kids.

name: Crockpot Chicken Pot Pie with Biscuits
steps: Add chicken, soup, broth and garlic powder to Crockpot. Cook LOW 5 hr until 165°F.
Shred chicken in the pot, stir in frozen veggies, cook 30 min more.
Bake biscuits per can. Spoon filling over split biscuits.

name: Baked Ziti (Make 2, Freeze 1)
steps: Heat oven to 375°F. Boil pasta 2 min less than package says. Brown meat; stir in marinara and Italian seasoning.
Mix pasta with sauce and ricotta. Split between two 8x8 pans; top with mozzarella and Parmesan.
Bake one, covered, 20 min then uncovered 10 min. Cool, cover and freeze the second (bake from thawed, 35-40 min).
notes: One cook, two dinners. Makes 4 servings per pan.

name: Sheet-Pan Chicken Fajitas
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Slice chicken, peppers and onion into strips; toss with oil and seasoning on a sheet pan.
Roast 20-25 min until chicken is 165°F.
Serve in tortillas with cheese and sour cream.
notes: Keep some chicken unseasoned or roast it on its own corner for picky kids.

name: Big-Batch Chicken Nuggets (Freezer)
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Cut chicken into 1½-inch pieces.
Dip in beaten egg, then panko mixed with Parmesan and seasonings. Spread on 2 oiled sheet pans.
Bake 15-18 min, flipping once, until 165°F. Eat half; freeze the rest flat, then bag. Reheat at 400°F 10-12 min.
notes: Cheaper and better than boxed nuggets.

name: Prep Day: Big-Batch Shredded Chicken
steps: Add everything to Crockpot. Cook LOW 4-5 hr until 165°F.
Shred and portion into 2-cup containers with a little broth.
Fridge 3-4 days or freeze up to 3 months.
notes: Makes ~8 cups — covers quesadillas, fried rice, Alfredo, broccoli pasta, chicken noodle soup and lunches.

name: Prep Day: Batch-Browned Ground Beef
steps: Brown all the beef in a large pot with garlic powder and salt; drain.
Cool and portion into 1-lb bags (about 2½ cups each).
Fridge 3-4 days or freeze flat. Season per meal: taco, spaghetti, sloppy joes, nachos.

name: Prep Day: Big Pot of Rice
steps: Rinse rice. Combine with 6 cups water and 1 tsp salt; bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce to low, cook 18 min. Rest 5 min, fluff.
Cool quickly on a sheet pan, then portion. Fridge 4 days; freeze extra.
notes: Makes ~9 cups. Day-old rice is perfect for fried rice.

name: Prep Day: Sheet-Pan Roasted Veggies
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Cut veggies bite-size, toss each separately with oil, salt, garlic powder.
Roast on separate pans: potatoes 30 min, carrots 25 min, broccoli 15-18 min.
Portion into containers for dinners and lunches.
notes: Keep each veg separate — kids are more likely to eat them that way.

name: Freezer Breakfast Burritos
steps: Brown sausage; remove. Cook hash browns in the same pan until crisp.
Scramble eggs soft. Combine with sausage, potatoes and cheese; cool 10 min.
Fill and roll tortillas, wrap each in foil, freeze in a bag. Reheat: unwrap, wrap in paper towel, microwave 1½-2 min.
notes: Make a few 'just egg and cheese' for picky kids — mark the foil.

name: Ham & Cheese Egg Muffins
steps: Heat oven to 350°F. Grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
Whisk eggs, milk, salt and pepper. Divide ham and cheese into cups, pour egg over.
Bake 20-22 min until set. Fridge 4 days or freeze. Reheat 30-45 sec.

name: Sheet-Pan Pancakes
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Line and grease a sheet pan.
Mix pancake mix, milk and eggs; spread on pan. Sprinkle toppings in sections (plain section for picky kids).
Bake 12-15 min. Cut into squares; freeze extras and toast to reheat.

name: Overnight Oats Jars
steps: Divide oats, milk, yogurt and honey between 4 jars; stir.
Refrigerate overnight (keeps 4 days).
Top with fruit in the morning. Eat cold or microwave 1 min.
notes: Kid version: add a spoon of peanut butter and mini chocolate chips.

name: Banana Oat Muffins
steps: Heat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin tin.
Mash bananas; whisk in eggs, honey and butter. Stir in flour, oats, baking soda and a pinch of salt; fold in chips.
Bake 18-22 min. Freeze extras.
notes: Waste-saver: use the bananas no one ate this week.

name: Freezer French Toast Sticks
steps: Heat oven to 400°F. Cut each slice into 3 sticks.
Dip in egg, milk, cinnamon and vanilla; set on a greased sheet pan.
Bake 15-18 min, flipping halfway. Freeze; reheat in toaster or air fryer.

name: Yogurt Parfait Bar
steps: Set out yogurt, granola and fruit.
Kids build their own cups.

name: Weekday Eggs & Toast Plate
steps: Scramble eggs low and slow with a pinch of salt; add cheese at the end.
Toast bread, cut into strips.
Serve with fruit.

name: Blackstone Smash Burgers
steps: Roll beef into 12 loose 2-oz balls. Heat griddle to high (~450°F). Butter and toast buns; set aside.
Place balls on griddle, smash flat with a spatula (parchment between helps), season with salt and pepper. Add thin onion on top if using.
Cook 2 min until crusty, flip, add cheese, cook 1 min. Stack 2 per bun.
notes: Kids: single patty with cheese, ketchup only. Air-fry tots alongside.

name: Blackstone Hibachi Chicken & Fried Rice
steps: Heat griddle to medium-high. Cut chicken bite-size. Oil griddle.
Cook chicken with 1 tbsp butter, salt, pepper, garlic powder and a splash of soy 6-8 min to 165°F; move to cool side. Cook onion and zucchini on another zone.
Fried rice: scramble eggs, add rice, peas/carrots, 2 tbsp butter and soy; toss until hot and crispy. Serve with yum yum sauce.
notes: Day-old rice works best — use Prep Day rice. Kids get chicken + plain-ish rice.

name: Blackstone Philly Cheesesteaks
steps: Heat griddle to medium-high. Cook sliced onion and pepper in oil 5-6 min.
Add steak, season with salt, pepper and garlic powder; chop with spatulas 3-4 min until browned. Mix in veggies (leave some plain for kids).
Divide into 4 piles, top with cheese, cover 1 min to melt. Scoop into toasted rolls.
notes: Chicken Philly: swap thin-sliced chicken breast.

name: Blackstone Big Breakfast
steps: Heat griddle to medium. Cook bacon on one side; push to the cool zone.
Spread hash browns in the bacon fat; cook 5 min per side until crispy. Mix pancake batter and pour pancakes on another zone.
Crack eggs last; cook to order. Serve everything family-style.
notes: Weekend morning or breakfast-for-dinner night.

name: Blackstone Chicken Lo Mein
steps: Boil noodles until just tender; drain and toss with sesame oil. Mix soy, brown sugar and minced garlic.
Heat griddle to medium-high. Cook bite-size chicken 6-8 min to 165°F. Add veggies 2-3 min.
Add noodles and sauce; toss 2 min until glossy.
notes: Set aside buttered noodles + plain chicken for picky kids.

name: Blackstone Smash Burger Tacos
steps: Heat griddle to medium-high. Roll beef into 8 balls.
Put a ball on each tortilla, smash flat across it, sprinkle with taco seasoning. Flip meat-side down; cook 2-3 min until crusty.
Flip, add cheese, fold. Top with lettuce, pickles and sauce.
notes: TikTok-famous and a big kid hit.

name: Blackstone Quesadilla Night
ingredients: cooked shredded chicken or taco meat
steps: Heat griddle to medium.
Lay out tortillas, add cheese and fillings to half, fold.
Cook 2-3 min per side until golden. Cook 4-6 at once.
notes: Uses Prep Day chicken or leftover taco meat.

name: Traeger Smoked Pulled Pork
steps: Smear pork with mustard, coat with rub. Smoke at 225-250°F until internal hits ~165°F (6-8 hr).
Wrap in foil with ½ cup apple juice; raise to 275°F. Cook until 200-203°F and probe-tender (3-4 hr).
Rest wrapped 1 hr. Shred, mix in some juices. Sauce on the side.
notes: Huge yield — freeze in 1-lb bags for nachos, quesadillas, BBQ pizza and sliders on future weeks.

name: Traeger Spatchcock Chicken
steps: Cut out the backbone with kitchen shears and press the chicken flat. Pat dry, rub with butter and rub.
Smoke at 225°F for 30 min, then raise to 375°F. Cook until thigh is 175°F and breast 160-165°F (about 1 hr more).
Rest 10 min. Roast potatoes on the grill alongside.
notes: Shred leftovers for next-day quesadillas or soup.

name: Traeger Smoked Drumsticks or Wings
steps: Pat chicken dry; toss with oil and rub.
Smoke at 225°F for 30 min, then raise to 400°F and cook 30-40 min until 175-185°F and crispy.
Toss half in sauce; leave half plain for the kids.
notes: Drumsticks are the cheapest chicken cut — big money saver.

name: Traeger Smoked Meatloaf
steps: Mix beef, eggs, breadcrumbs, milk, garlic and onion powder, salt and pepper. Shape a loaf on a foil-lined tray.
Smoke at 225°F for 1 hr, then raise to 350°F.
Brush with ketchup-sugar glaze; cook until 160°F (45-60 min more). Rest 10 min. Serve with mashed potatoes.
notes: Leftover meatloaf sandwiches = great lunches.

name: Traeger Smoked Cheeseburgers
steps: Form 6 patties, press a thumbprint in the center, season.
Smoke at 225°F for 25-30 min, then raise to 450°F (or move to Blackstone) and sear 2-3 min per side to 160°F.
Add cheese the last minute.

name: Traeger Brown Sugar Pork Tenderloin
steps: Coat tenderloins with oil, rub and brown sugar.
Smoke at 250°F until 135°F inside (~45 min).
Brush with honey, raise to 400°F and sear to 145°F. Rest 5 min, slice.
notes: Lean, cheap, and it tastes 'like ham' to kids.

name: Traeger Smoked Mac & Cheese
steps: Cook macaroni 2 min short. Make cheese sauce: butter + flour 1 min, whisk in milk until thick, stir in 2½ cups cheese.
Mix with pasta in a foil pan; top with remaining cheese.
Smoke at 225°F for 30 min, then 350°F for 15-20 min until bubbly.
notes: Perfect side for pulled pork or drumsticks night.

name: Traeger Pizza Night
steps: Preheat Traeger to 450-500°F with a pizza stone or pan inside for 20 min.
Stretch dough, top with sauce, cheese, toppings (kids make their own).
Bake 10-14 min until crust is golden.
notes: Leftover pulled pork + BBQ sauce makes a great adult pizza.

name: Honey Mustard Baked Chicken Thighs
steps: Heat oven to 400°F. Whisk honey, mustard, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Toss chicken in sauce in a baking dish.
Bake 25-30 min until 175°F. Serve over rice with broccoli; spoon pan sauce over.

name: Parmesan Crusted Chicken
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Spread a thin layer of mayo on chicken.
Press into Parmesan, panko and garlic powder. Bake on a sheet pan 15-20 min to 165°F.
Serve with buttered or marinara spaghetti.
notes: Mayo keeps it super juicy; kids don't taste it.

name: Cheesy Chicken & Rice Casserole
steps: Heat oven to 350°F. Mix chicken, rice, soup, sour cream, broccoli and 1½ cups cheese.
Spread in a 9x13; top with remaining cheese and crushed Ritz.
Bake 25-30 min until bubbly.
notes: Uses Prep Day chicken + rice. Freezes well.

name: Oven BBQ Drumsticks
ingredients: BBQ rub or paprika + garlic powder
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss drumsticks with oil and rub on a foil-lined sheet pan.
Bake 35 min, flipping once.
Brush with BBQ sauce; bake 10 min more until 175°F+. Serve with corn.
notes: One of the cheapest dinners in the book.

name: Crockpot Family Chili
steps: Brown beef and diced onion; drain.
Add to Crockpot with drained beans, tomatoes, sauce and seasoning. Cook LOW 6-8 hr.
Serve with cheese and cornbread. Leftovers: chili dogs or Frito pie.
notes: Mild packet keeps it kid-safe; adults add hot sauce.

name: Crockpot Taco Soup
steps: Brown beef; drain.
Dump everything (don't drain cans except beans) into the Crockpot with 1 cup water. Cook LOW 6 hr.
Serve with chips, cheese, and sour cream.
notes: Dump-and-go. Great thermos lunch.

name: Crockpot Lasagna Soup
steps: Brown meat; drain. Add to Crockpot with marinara, broth and Italian seasoning. Cook LOW 6 hr.
Break noodles into pieces, stir in, cook HIGH 30 min until tender.
Top bowls with a spoon of ricotta and mozzarella.

name: Crockpot Chicken & Gravy
steps: Whisk gravy mix, soup and water in Crockpot; add chicken.
Cook LOW 5-6 hr until 165°F. Shred or slice.
Serve over mashed potatoes with green beans.

name: Crockpot Ground Beef Stroganoff
steps: Brown beef; drain. Add to Crockpot with soup, broth and onion soup mix. Cook LOW 4 hr.
Stir in cubed cream cheese and sour cream until smooth.
Serve over egg noodles.

name: Homemade Cheeseburger Pasta (Better Hamburger Helper)
steps: Brown beef in a large skillet; drain.
Add broth, milk, ketchup, mustard, garlic powder and dry macaroni. Bring to a boil, cover, simmer 10-12 min, stirring, until pasta is tender.
Stir in cheddar off heat.
notes: One pan. Tastes like a cheeseburger — kids usually love it.

name: Cottage Pie (Ground Beef Shepherd's Pie)
steps: Boil peeled potatoes until tender; mash with butter, milk, salt.
Brown beef and diced onion; drain. Stir in gravy mix + 1 cup water and veggies; simmer 5 min.
Spread in a 9x13, top with mashed potatoes and cheese. Bake at 400°F 20 min.
notes: Use Mississippi roast or leftover mashed potatoes to save time.

name: Freezer Beef & Bean Burritos
steps: Brown beef with taco seasoning and ½ cup water.
Warm tortillas. Spread beans, add rice, beef and cheese. Roll tightly.
Wrap each in foil and freeze. Microwave 2-3 min (unwrapped, in paper towel) or bake at 375°F 25 min.
notes: Easy lunches all week. Make some 'bean & cheese only'.

name: Korean Ground Beef Bowls
steps: Brown beef with minced garlic; drain.
Stir in soy, brown sugar and sesame oil; simmer 2 min.
Serve over rice with veggies.
notes: Sweet-salty — similar to teriyaki, usually kid approved.

name: Tater Tot Casserole
ingredients: cream of mushroom or chicken soup
frozen green beans or mixed veg
steps: Heat oven to 375°F. Brown beef; drain. Stir in soup, sour cream and veggies.
Spread in 9x13, top with cheese then tots in rows.
Bake 35-40 min until tots are crispy.

name: Harvest Chicken
steps: Spread the squash, apples, and onion across the bottom of the slow cooker. Place the chicken on top.
Stir the broth, maple syrup, Dijon, and sage together, then pour over the chicken.
Cover and cook on HIGH for 3½ hours or LOW for 6 hours. Slice the chicken and serve with the squash and apples.
notes: Creator-reported protein: 44 g per serving. Serving size not specified.

name: Turkey Tenderloin with Sage Gravy
cook: HIGH 3 hr or LOW 5½ hr + 10 min HIGH for gravy
steps: Put the sweet potatoes and onion in the slow cooker. Add the turkey, broth, sage, and garlic powder.
Cover and cook on HIGH for 3 hours or LOW for 5½ hours. Transfer the turkey to a plate.
Whisk the cornstarch into the cooking liquid. Cook on HIGH for 10 minutes to thicken.
Stir in the Greek yogurt and spoon the gravy over the sliced turkey and vegetables.
notes: Creator-reported protein: 48 g per serving. Serving size not specified.

name: Smothered Pork Chops
cook: LOW 4–5 hr + 15 min HIGH for sauce
steps: Add the pork chops, mushrooms, broth, garlic, and thyme to the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on LOW for 4–5 hours, then transfer the chops to a plate.
Whisk the cornstarch into the liquid in the cooker and cook on HIGH for 15 minutes.
Stir in the Greek yogurt and spoon the mushroom sauce over the chops.
notes: Creator-reported protein: 54 g per serving. Serving size not specified.

name: Spinach Artichoke Chicken
steps: Add the chicken, artichoke hearts, broth, and garlic to the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on LOW for 4–5 hours, then shred the chicken.
Stir in the cream cheese, spinach, and Parmesan. Cover and cook for another 15 minutes, then stir before serving.
notes: Creator-reported protein: 60 g per serving. Serving size not specified.

name: Garlic Butter Steak and Potatoes
steps: Spread the potatoes across the bottom of the slow cooker and add the cubed sirloin on top.
Stir together the melted butter, garlic, broth, Italian seasoning, and smoked paprika. Pour over the steak and potatoes.
Cover and cook on LOW for 5 hours or HIGH for 3 hours.
notes: Creator-reported protein: 53 g per serving. Serving size not specified.
